newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. renews 125-member observer mission in Georgia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. renews 125-member observer mission in Georgia.

text.p: The Security Council unanimously approved on Thursday a six-month renewal of the 125-member U.N. Observer Mission in Georgia (UNOMIG) where negotiations between the government and Abkhazian separatists remained deadlocked.
About 250,000 Georgians fled the Abkhazia region of Georgia in 1993 when separatists backed by mercenaries and arms from Russia's northern Caucasus drove out government troops.
Occasional violence has since punctuated an uneasy calm enforced by Russian-led peacekeepers fielded by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
Still unresolved are issues concerning the future status of Abkhazia and the return of refugees.
In extending the U.N. observer mission until July 31, the Security Council said this was subject to review if any changes were made in the mandate of the CIS peacekeeping force.

The council reaffirmed its commitment to Georgia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, within its internationally recognised borders, and said Abkhazia's status must be defined in strict accordance with those principles.

The council underlined the "unacceptability of any action by the Abkhaz leadership in contravention of those principles," particularly the holding last November and December of "illegitimate and self-styled parliamentary elections" in the breakaway region.
It welcomed the intention of Secretary-General Kofi Annan, as outlined in a recent report, to initiate contacts in the region with both sides to help them unblock the peace process.
Ambassador Edouard Brunner, a Swiss diplomat, is the U.N. chief's special envoy for Abkhazia.
Annan's report noted the parties themselves recently held high-level bilateral meetings and called this an encouraging development.
The council resolution also condemned the continued laying of mines -- includes new types -- in the Gali sector, one of the security and restricted weapons zones where the U.N. observers operate.

It said the mines had already caused several deaths and injuries among the civilian population as well as among peacekeepers and observers, and called on the parties to take all possible measures to prevent mine laying and intensified activities by armed groups.
